title: I Took the Silent Auction Bid Sheet to the Charity Chair

parts.text: I watched her erase my bid and write her sister's number in the same pencil. I am forty-one, teacher in a too-tight gala dress, feet angry. The item was a weekend cabin donated by a parent. I had bid $420, a stretch. Chairwoman Lila smiled with wine teeth. The ballroom carpet had a sticky soda patch I kept hitting. Lila said, "Your bid wasn't valid ink" I said, "It's the pencil you provided" My friend Nate saw the eraser crumbs. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Eraser crumbs are on the bid sheet, and her sister's number is in my $420 slot.

social.description: Sticky carpet, wine teeth, and a pencil they handed out. $420 was a stretch. Would you have grabbed the sheet?

parts.text: I took the sheet to the auctioneer, a bored man named Cal with a real mic. Cal announced a dispute, which Lila hated because it had a sound. The parent who donated the cabin, Rosa, asked to see the sheet. Eraser crumbs do not lie well. Rosa withdrew the cabin from the silent table and gifted a school weekend instead, to the school, not the sister. Lila called me disruptive. Nate posted the crumbs photo in the volunteer chat. I went home, took off the dress, ate cereal. The soda patch stayed on the carpet. I still volunteer, but I bring a pen. Ink is a boundary. Cal said, "Who changed this number" Lila said, "It was a clarification" Rosa emailed thanks. The kids get the cabin weekend. That is the point.
